name: stage-warp-lens
summary: a generic stage of mocha-stage: a lens distortion applied to or removed from each frame, with the lens-model crate for the coordinates and the resample crate for the samples; a published method under explicit configuration, not compared with any product

binaries.name: mocha-stage
binaries.arguments: apply warp-lens --width W --height H --depth 8|16|32 --fps N[/D] [--frames N] [--describe] [--param K=V]... [--layer keys=PATH]
binaries.stdin: whole raw frames; not read with --describe
binaries.stdout: the frames of the stage, nothing else; with --describe one line of JSON
binaries.stderr: empty on exit 0; exactly one line error: CODE: MESSAGE on a failure

frame_contract: frames/2 raw frames: depth 8 is packed rgba (4 bytes per pixel), depth 16 is packed rgba64le (8 bytes), depth 32 is planar gbrapf32le (16 bytes, planes G, B, R, A, 1.0 is full scale); whole frames back to back, no header, no padding, straight alpha, a frame of at most 4 GiB; a stream that ends inside a frame is a partial frame

parameters.maps_to: Output width in pixels; 0 keeps the input width.
Output height in pixels; 0 keeps the input height.

parameters.accepts: nearest, bilinear, keys, mitchell, lanczos, box
parameters.maps_to: The reconstruction filter (Config::filter).
The parameter a of the Keys cubic; read when filter is keys.
The parameter B of the Mitchell and Netravali cubic; read when filter is mitchell.
The parameter C of the Mitchell and Netravali cubic; read when filter is mitchell.
The lobes per side of the Lanczos filter; read when filter is lanczos.
What a tap outside the image reads (Config::border).
Whether pixel i has its centre at i + 0.5 or at i (Config::center).
Whether colour is interpolated as it is or multiplied by alpha first and divided afterwards (Config::alpha).
Whether the result is divided by the sum of the tap weights (Config::normalize).
Where the nearest filter goes when the coordinate is halfway between two pixels (Config::tie).
The order of the accumulation loop, which matters for rounding only (Config::order).
The size of the box filter in source pixels: one pixel, or the mapped output pixel (Config::footprint).
Whether the stage makes a distorted frame from an undistorted one or the reverse (Direction).
The distortion model: the radial polynomial with tangential terms, the division model, or the radial polynomial on squeezed axes (Model).
The first radial coefficient; read by radial and squeezed; may be keyed.
The second radial coefficient; read by radial and squeezed; may be keyed.
The third radial coefficient; read by radial and squeezed; may be keyed.
The first tangential coefficient; read by radial; may be keyed.
The second tangential coefficient; read by radial; may be keyed.
The parameter of the division model; read by division; may be keyed.
The factor on x inside the radius; read by squeezed.
The factor on y inside the radius; read by squeezed.
What pixel offsets from the centre are divided by (Config::normalisation).
The divisor when normalisation is focal-length.
The distortion centre as a fraction of the input width (Config::centre); may be keyed.
The distortion centre as a fraction of the input height (Config::centre); may be keyed.
The width of a pixel over its height (Config::pixel_aspect).
Which way the formula of the model goes (Config::maps).
How the inverse of the formula is computed where the stage needs it (Config::inverse_method); closed-form exists for division only.
The fixed step count of the iterative inverse methods (Config::inverse_iterations).

layers.meaning: A key file with a value per frame for k1, k2, k3, p1, p2, lambda, centre_x and centre_y.

geometry: declared: the output is width by height, where 0 keeps the input side; the frame count, the depth and the rate are those of the request; --describe answers the output geometry without reading standard input and without opening a layer; a keyed parameter never changes the geometry; the output canvas is centred on the input frame
sample_rule: computed on f32 samples: an integer sample v is v / 255 or v / 65535, computed in f64 and rounded once to f32; on the way out a sample x is floor(clamp(x, 0, 1) * max + 0.5) and a sample that is not a number is 0; depth 32 samples are the stream's own floats and are never clamped; each output pixel is sampled by the resample crate at the source position the map of the stage gives for it, under the filter, border, pixel centre, alpha and normalisation rule of the parameters; a pixel without a source position is zero in all four channels; the map is Config::source_map of the lens-model crate for the direction, with the input frame as the image of the model and the centre given as a fraction of its width and height
error_line: error: CODE: MESSAGE, one line on standard error, where CODE is usage, unsupported, bad_input, partial_frame, broken_pipe or stage_failed

exit_codes_table.means: every input frame was processed and written, or --describe printed its answer
stage_failed: the output could not be written for a reason other than a closed pipe
usage: a bad or missing option, a parameter or a layer given twice, a layer with an empty path
unsupported: a depth the stage does not take, a parameter or a layer the stage does not have, a value the stage refuses, a transform or a layer content the configuration refuses
bad_input, partial_frame or broken_pipe: a failed read, input that ends inside a frame, a frame count other than --frames, a layer file that cannot be read or parsed, a reader that went away
exit_codes_table.table: the table's bad_input, partial_frame and broken_pipe

unpinned_paths.why: a write to standard output that fails for a reason other than a closed pipe; no test makes one, because it needs a device that differs between systems
a reader that closes the pipe while the stage writes; tests/stage_<id>.rs and the convention's conformance tool exercise it, the rows of this file do not
